sections.heading: Greenhouse buyer question and thesis
sections.body:
applicant tracking; career site and job boards; interview scheduling; core hris. Core · applicant tracking | Plus | Pro. Slack, Linkedin, Google Workspace. Mid-market and enterprise teams that want structured hiring (kits, scorecards, governance); Talent orgs comparing Greenhouse as the default dedicated ATS; Companies that will integrate ATS to an existing HRIS/payroll rather than buying all-in-one HR. Greenhouse is a structured-hiring ATS/CRM from sourcing through offer and onboarding, with interview kits, scorecards, scheduling, and recruiting analytics. Named plans are Core, P. That catalogue mix is the Greenhouse setup filter — not a generic hr lecture.

Buyer question: for applicant tracking teams, is Greenhouse worth the Core unlock, or does No published list price — quotes scale with hiring volume and complexity, not recruiter seats alone kill the rollout?

ROI gate: Greenhouse is worth the Core spend if applicant tracking + career site and job boards are weekly; not worth buying when No published list price — quotes scale with hiring volume and complexity, not recruiter seats alone.

Best for: Mid-market and enterprise teams that want structured hiring (kits, scorecards, governance); Talent orgs comparing Greenhouse as the default dedicated ATS; Companies that will integrate ATS to an existing HRIS/payroll rather than buying all-in-one HR (Mid-market and enterprise teams that want structured hiring (kits, scorecards, governance)).

Poor fit when: SMB teams that need a free ATS tier (Breezy Bootstrap); Buyers whose primary job is core HRIS or payroll; Frontline scheduling / time-clock operators. Avoid if No published list price — quotes scale with hiring volume and complexity, not recruiter seats alone would block go-live.

sections.heading: Greenhouse limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: No published list price — quotes scale with hiring volume and complexity, not recruiter seats alone; Implementation and onboarding modules are often separate commercially; AI/enterprise features are gated by tier because it forces process changes or add-ons around Greenhouse when applicant tracking is the job.

Pricing interpretation: no free plan confirmed — scope a paid pilot on Core with exit criteria before annual seats.

Plan trade-off: you gain applicant tracking at the expense of Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Core · applicant tracking | Plus | Pro.

Alternative context: unlike Breezy HR, Greenhouse is preferable when Mid-market and enterprise teams that want structured hiring (kits, scorecards, governance) because applicant tracking plus applicant tracking match; prefer Breezy HR when SMB teams that need a free ATS tier (Breezy Bootstrap) because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Greenhouse
sections.body:
Workflow advantage: Greenhouse is faster for applicant tracking when applicant tracking; career site and job boards; interview scheduling; core hris is in-product; skip when No published list price — quotes scale with hiring volume and complexity, not recruiter seats alone because that loop lives elsewhere.

Implementation complexity: setup requires confirming applicant tracking ownership and Slack before rollout — do not scale seats first.

Integrations in research: Slack, Linkedin, Google Workspace.

Conclusion: Greenhouse is worth it if Mid-market and enterprise teams that want structured hiring (kits, scorecards, governance) and applicant tracking are weekly; skip Greenhouse if SMB teams that need a free ATS tier (Breezy Bootstrap). That is the decision, not a template with the logo swapped.
